quote: Kann man auch direkt dasselbe zeigen, wenn an Stelle der Differen- tialgleichung $\Delta F=0$ irgend eine andere algebraische Diffe- rentialgl zwischen den ersten, [-...-] $2^{\text{ten}}$, $3^{\text{ten}}$ .. Differential- quotienten besteht?
english: Can one also show the same directly if, in place of the differential equation ΔF=0, some other algebraic differential equation holds between the first, second, third ... derivatives?
topic: Three short notes: questions on the discriminant of a quadratic form built from the roots of an algebraic equation (the equation with real roots in lambda), a question on directly proving regularity of solutions of differential equations other than Laplace's, and the problem of counting the possible configurations of n circles in the plane.

triage.modern_statement: Harmonic functions (solutions of ΔF=0) are known to be real-analytic. The note asks whether that same regularity can be proved directly when F satisfies some other algebraic, or more generally analytic, PDE F(x, u, Du, D²u, D³u, …)=0 instead of Laplace's equation. In modern terms: is every sufficiently smooth solution of a nonlinear analytic PDE real-analytic? The precise modern answer is that this holds when the equation is elliptic, but not for arbitrary equations, since hyperbolic equations such as the wave equation have non-analytic smooth solutions. One caveat: the page only says 'dasselbe' (the same), so reading it as analyticity is an inference from the page topic.
triage.answered_by: This question became Hilbert's 19th problem (Paris, 1900). Positive answers: S. Bernstein (1904) for C^3 solutions of analytic nonlinear elliptic equations in two variables; E. Hopf (1932) for C^2 solutions in any dimension; I. G. Petrowsky (1939) for analytic nonlinear elliptic systems of general order. The weak-solution/variational version was settled by De Giorgi (1957) and Nash (1958), and the result is now called the De Giorgi–Nash–Moser theory. For non-elliptic equations the answer is no.

evidence.claim: Hilbert's 19th problem is a regularity problem for elliptic PDEs with analytic coefficients. It was solved independently in the late 1950s by De Giorgi and Nash, and Bernstein had earlier answered it for C^3 solutions.
Hopf proved analyticity of C^2 solutions in any dimension, and Petrowsky generalized this to systems of elliptic PDEs.
Nash's Hölder estimates, proved in parallel with De Giorgi, solved Hilbert's 19th problem on the analyticity of minimizers of analytic elliptic integral functionals.

Petrowsky's 1939 paper 'Sur l'analyticité des solutions des systèmes d'équations différentielles' is still cited, and new proofs of analyticity for analytic nonlinear elliptic systems are still being published (arXiv 2025).

triage.why: The note asks whether the analyticity known for solutions of ΔF=0 carries over to other algebraic differential equations. That is the core of what Hilbert published in 1900 as his 19th problem, there restricted to regular variational problems, whose Euler–Lagrange equations are analytic elliptic PDEs. Bernstein, Hopf and Petrowsky settled the classical case, and De Giorgi and Nash settled the weak-solution case. As stated, the note's 'any algebraic differential equation' is too broad: the result needs ellipticity. Elliptic regularity theory remains an active field, with new proofs still appearing in 2025. Confidence is medium rather than high because the page only says 'dasselbe' and never names analyticity, so linking the note to the 19th problem is a strong inference, not something the page says outright.
